name: Nova Default AI
author: Galaxies core team
description: The classic Stars! Nova AI: expands, scouts, colonizes. Plays against the engine's own object graph via native intel.
determinism_note: The guarantee holds: replaying the same empire_view yields byte-identical orders. The mechanism is not seeding. The AI sources (Nova/Ai/AbstractAI.cs, DefaultAi.cs, DefaultAIPlanner.cs, DefaultFleetAI.cs, DefaultPlanetAI.cs) contain no Random, no Guid, no clock read, and no hash-derived branch, so there is no randomness for the seat seed to constrain. The worker parses game.seat_seed and reports it in diagnostics.seed_used, and says in diagnostics.notes that nothing consumed it. If randomness is ever added, the injection point is DefaultAi.DoMove, which constructs the planner and the per-planet and per-fleet AIs; each would take a Random built from the seat seed, and this field would then describe a mechanism rather than a property.
native_intel_note: This participant requires intel_native on the dispatch. It reconstructs a real Nova.Common.Intel with Envelope.ReadIntel and plays the authoritative graph. It deliberately does NOT reconstruct an EmpireData from the lossy empire_view projection: guessing the dropped fields would make it a quietly weaker opponent than the desktop AI it claims to be. Dispatched without intel_native it returns an empty orders list and says why in diagnostics.
